output.brief: The Android login drop is not caused by release 6.14. It was caused by a new edge-protection rule that Corvane pushed on 3 March at 10:38 UTC. The rule (AUTO-LIB-17) blocks any request from the app's networking library (nettle-http) to the password-login path when there is no edge session cookie. Every Android app version uses that library, so every version is hit. The block began at 10:41, about 3 minutes after the rule pack went live. It returns HTTP 403 and now blocks roughly 9,600 requests a day. The blocked requests come from about 41,300 installs, and 92% of those installs had logged in successfully in the prior 90 days. They are real customers. Quick-unlock, iOS and web are untouched. Success is the same, about 88%, on 6.14 and older versions, on every OS version, and with or without the March security patch. That rules out a 6.14 defect and a phone-update cause. The credential-stuffing and token-lifetime explanations also do not fit this pattern. Next steps: 1) Ask Corvane today to set the new rules to log-only on the mobile password path. Keep rate limits, lockout and the other rules on. 2) Confirm in telemetry that Android password success returns to about 96%. 3) Do not roll back 6.14. Do not raise bot sensitivity. Do not exclude blocked attempts from the KPI. 4) Agree a change process with Corvane so rule updates are tested against the mobile app. I am fairly sure of this diagnosis. The contact-centre link is still only an association, because the call rise also overlaps the fee notices.
